name: Jeswanth Posina
summary: Second-year ECE student at VIT-AP focused on Android application security: static and dynamic analysis, reverse engineering and binary patching with JADX, APKTool and ADB, following OWASP MASTG. Competed in L3AK CTF 2026 and contribute to the Null InfoSec chapter. Seeking an Application Security Engineer role.

entries.degree: B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering

entries.title: Android Application Security Assessment (AndroGoat)
bullets: Performed static analysis with JADX to locate hardcoded secrets (API keys, promo codes, tokens) embedded in a vulnerable Android APK.
Identified insecure local data storage in SharedPreferences by combining static analysis with dynamic inspection via ADB.
Documented client-side trust risks and secure-storage recommendations based on OWASP Mobile Top 10 principles.

entries.title: Binary Patching & Privilege Escalation Challenge
bullets: Reverse engineered an Android APK to locate client-side isAdmin authorization check using JADX.
Modified application logic with APKTool, rebuilt and re-signed the APK, and escalated privileges on an emulator, proving client-side authorization bypass.

entries.title: Network Security Fundamentals & Lab Work
bullets: Configured and verified a subnetted network topology in Cisco Packet Tracer to reinforce IP addressing and routing concepts.
Analyzed HTTP traffic and firewall/ACL behavior using Wireshark and Nmap on a self-hosted IIS server, comparing ICMP versus HTTPS handling.

entries.title: L3AK CTF 2026 (International Capture the Flag Competition)
bullets: Competed in a 48-hour international CTF solving GeoOSINT and CSRF-bypass challenges under competitive conditions.
Conducted HTTP request analysis and client-side JavaScript injection testing.
Analyzed official write-ups for unsolved challenges to expand exploitation methodologies.
Contribute to a student-run information security community focused on ethical hacking, CTF challenges, and security awareness.
